result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers recommend B and explain that a multiple-choice test shows a rep can recognize a good answer, not give one. A handles the team lead's time better: it works out a concrete plan that cuts about 15 hours to about 5 (the lead runs one role-play per rep, peers run the other two, and the lead's sessions are in groups) and adds a scalable knowledge check for the VP. B's ideas are reasonable but vaguer. It never says how many hours the lead saves, and its fallback of two live rounds would still take about 10 hours of the lead's time. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers recommend B and explain clearly that picking a multiple-choice answer shows recognition, not the ability to deliver a response live. B handles the time constraint better: it brings the lead's load from 15 hours to about 5 by having peers run two of the rounds, and suggests group sessions. B also gives the VP a concrete scalable piece, a 10-question pre-check on product and pricing facts. A's rubric and co-scoring ideas are good, but it never says how many hours it saves, it leaves a placeholder ('[current appointment-set or close rate]') in the text, and B's only weak spot is a fallback that cuts peer rounds, which doesn't free up any of the lead's time.
